pathways.notes: Synthetic alternative: people remain in place while a declared water-capacity intervention is tested. This is not an intervention recommendation.
Synthetic alternative: 1,000 persons arrive at destination-b. The count is a scenario input, not observed or forecast migration.

assumptions.statement: The in-place adaptation alternative adds 40 m3/day of synthetic reliable potable delivery capacity. This is arithmetic test data, not a costed or feasible engineering intervention.
The voluntary-movement alternative declares 1,000 arrivals as a scenario input. It is not an empirical count, probability, forecast or recommendation.
The synthetic incremental potable-water demand is 0.05 m3/person/day. This is a fixture constant only, not a normative service threshold or local demand estimate.
The synthetic household conversion is 0.5 additional households per arriving person; it is not a demographic estimate.

limitations: No real geographic boundaries, coordinates, climate forcing, population observations, migration events, utility data or community preferences are represented.
Only drinking-water delivery and habitable-household capacity are included; all other service domains remain unassessed.
The expected outcomes test arithmetic and contract behavior only. They do not establish potable-water safety, housing habitability or receiving-place suitability.
The fixture does not assign probabilities to pathways and does not infer climate attribution.
The service-floor example is synthetic-only: its arbitrary threshold is not a real minimum service standard, and its partial coverage cannot support a full-scope floor verdict.
claim_ceiling: Synthetic arithmetic and schema behavior only; not a real city assessment, migration forecast, engineering validation or relocation recommendation.

limitations: The threshold and measurement units are arbitrary synthetic contract constants, not a legal or community-approved service standard.
Only 10 of 100 synthetic coverage units are represented; the observed breach must not be generalized to the full service scope.
No actual water-delivery, health, affordability, or household measurement is represented.

Synthetic/contract-only floor evidence must remain Indeterminate in the executable evaluator; the partial-breach arithmetic is exercised by unit tests using explicit reference-matched test inputs, not promoted from this fixture.
